response.consequence: After a concurrent create, update or remove of a login IDP, login IDP lists for other organizations or fetch modes can stay stale. Newly added IDPs would be missing from login, or removed IDPs would keep being listed until the next invalidation. The window is narrow, but the staleness is not self-healing.
response.explanation: In getForLogin, and in the same-shaped branch of getByOrganization, a request that misses on its searchKey does the following. It reads the existing IdentityProviderListQuery. It calls invalidateObject(cacheKey), which bumps the revision. It then builds a new IdentityProviderListQuery that copies all of the previous query's searchKeys (IdentityProviderListQuery constructor, lines 39-45). It stores the result with addRevisioned(query, cache.getCurrentCounter()). Suppose another transaction commits an invalidation of this key after the earlier cache.get(cacheKey) and before this invalidateObject. The previous object is then already stale, but its sets for other searchKeys (for example other organization ids) are copied into an entry carrying the new, current revision. addRevisioned's checks cannot reject it. The startup revision is taken as the current counter after the bump, so it passes the "rev > startupRevision" check. The revision equals the object's revision, so the entry is cached. The stale sets for the other searchKeys now survive as valid until the next invalidation. Other providers use the loaded revision or startupRevision and never merge pre-invalidation data.
response.title: Merging a previously cached query into a fresh-revision entry can resurrect stale IDP id sets

response.consequence: IDPs such as idp-alias-0..20 and their org links can leak into later tests. The cleanup step can also throw NotFound during teardown, which makes the test brittle.
